_comment: The demo set. Each page is hand-written: no scripts, no external resources,
nothing captured from a real attacker. The hostname matters as much as the
markup, because half the rules read the URL, so each entry names the host it
must be served from and what it is expected to trigger.
Ports 80, 443 and 8080 are the standard set. Serving on 80 keeps the URL free
of a port, so non_standard_port stays quiet and every rule that fires does so

pages.why: high-abuse TLD, brand named in the page but not in its domain, form posts to another host, and the language classifier reads it as phishing
high-abuse TLD, DHL named off-domain, card fields posting to a third host
an ordinary-looking page on an ordinary domain; only the injection rule fires, and the decision floor lifts it to Warn on its own
a real-looking local library: nothing should fire at all
